title: Route Refresh Capability for BGP-4
summary: Defines a Border Gateway Protocol capability that lets one BGP speaker ask another to resend its routes. This allows a policy change to take effect without resetting the connection. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: BGP route refresh lets one router ask a peer to send its routes again. This can apply a changed routing policy without keeping a separate unchanged copy of every route.

questions: how to re-request bgp routes without reset
how does bgp route refresh work
what does a route refresh message contain
subtitle: Lets BGP peers request a fresh advertisement of routes after policy changes.

tldr.problem: After an inbound routing policy changes, a BGP speaker needs the peer's routes again, but keeping an unmodified copy of every route uses extra memory and CPU.
tldr.mechanism: Peers advertise a Route Refresh capability. A speaker that has received it can request a refresh for an address family, and the peer re-advertises matching routes under its outbound policy.
tldr.outcome: Route refresh can support policy changes without maintaining an unmodified route copy at all times. Unit metadata lists RFC 7313 as an update.

today: RFC 2918 is listed as a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 7313, according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: Refreshing Routes After a Change
sections.content:
When a router changes its inbound policy for a BGP peer, it needs to examine that peer's routes under the new policy. A common approach was to keep an unmodified copy of all routes continuously, which uses additional memory and CPU.

This RFC defines a capability that lets one BGP speaker ask its peer to re-advertise routes instead.
sections.plainLanguage: A router may need to reevaluate routes after its policy changes. Route refresh lets it ask its peer to send the routes again, avoiding a stored backup copy.

sections.title: Advertising the Capability
sections.content:
A BGP speaker advertises Route Refresh Capability using a BGP Capabilities Advertisement. The capability code is 2 and its length is 0.

Advertising the capability tells the peer that the speaker can receive and handle a ROUTE-REFRESH message. A speaker may send that message only after it has received the capability from its peer.
sections.plainLanguage: Each router tells its peer whether it can handle route-refresh requests. A router must not send a request until its peer has advertised that ability.

sections.title: The ROUTE-REFRESH Message
sections.content:
The new BGP message has type 5 and carries an Address Family Identifier (AFI), a reserved field, and a Subsequent Address Family Identifier (SAFI). Together, AFI and SAFI identify the address family of the routes to refresh.

The reserved field is 8 bits. The sender should set it to zero, and the receiver ignores it.
sections.plainLanguage: The request names the address family whose routes should be sent again. Its reserved field is set to zero by the sender and ignored by the receiver.

sections.title: Request and Re-advertisement
sections.content:
A speaker can request a refresh only for an AFI and SAFI that the peer advertised when the BGP session was established. If the peer receives a request for an unadvertised pair, it ignores the request.

For a valid request, the peer re-advertises its routes for that address family according to its outbound route-filtering policy.
sections.plainLanguage: The peer checks that the request names an address family it previously advertised. If it does, the peer sends the matching routes again under its current outbound policy.
